headline: CALEDONIA MINING UP 8.2%: K-PITS GOLD ZONE UNLOCKS HEAP LEACH OPTIONALITY AT BLANKET — Q2 PRODUCTION JUMPS 18%
source_name: Caledonia Mining Corp (NYSE: CMCL / TSX: CAL)
snippet: Caledonia Mining Corporation (NYSE: CMCL; TSX: CAL) released its Q2 2026 full financial results and a major exploration update on August 10, 2026: gold production at the Blanket Mine in Zimbabwe jumped 18% quarter-on-quarter to 17,360 ounces at an average grade of 2.88 g/t, with full-year guidance of 72,000–76,500 ounces reaffirmed. The bigger market reaction (+8.2% in early trading) was driven by the simultaneous release of Blanket Exploration Results identifying the K-Pits zone — a previously unrecognised near-surface gold occurrence with highlights including 23.00 metres at 2.61 g/t from surface — with both oxide and sulphide mineralisation confirmed. The oxide fraction is potentially amenable to heap leaching, and the company has flagged a proposed 10,000-tonne heap leach trial in H2 2026 pending acceptable recovery rates in bench testing. An updated Blanket mineral resource statement incorporating K-Pits is expected later in August 2026. For retail investors in a sub-$200M market cap gold producer operating at approximately $4,300 gold, the K-Pits discovery adds a second potential production pathway (lower-cost surface heap leach alongside the existing underground operation) to a mine that already holds Zimbabwe's primary gold producer designation — a material increase in the range of potential outcomes for existing shareholders.

headline: EQUINOX GOLD EQX: ORLA MERGER CLOSES, NORTH AMERICA'S NEW SENIOR PRODUCER TARGETS 870–920K OZ — DIVIDEND HIKED 50%
source_name: Equinox Gold (TSX: EQX / NYSE American: EQX)
snippet: Equinox Gold Corp (TSX: EQX; NYSE American: EQX) reported Q2 2026 results on August 5, 2026 alongside the formal completion of its transformational combination with Orla Mining on July 31 — a deal that Equinox CEO Jason Simpson described as creating North America's new senior gold producer. The combined entity has raised 2026 production guidance to 870,000–920,000 ounces (up from 700,000–800,000 ounces guidance for Equinox standalone), with a pro-forma annualised run-rate of approximately 1.1 million ounces if Orla's assets had been consolidated from January 1. The production portfolio is anchored by three long-life Canadian mines: Greenstone in Ontario (currently ramping up), Valentine in Newfoundland, and Musselwhite in Ontario, with Orla's Camino Rojo in Mexico adding substantial low-AISC production. The Q2 standalone Equinox print was strong — 176,836 ounces at record profitability — and approximately $650M in cash plus $1.2B in available liquidity provides the balance sheet capacity for the Valentine Phase 2 expansion and debt reduction. The board approved a 50% increase in the annual dividend to $0.09 per share. For retail investors tracking the gold M&A consolidation cycle, Equinox-Orla is the largest completed TSX gold producer combination of 2026 and positions the combined company as a natural acquisition target for Tier 1 majors seeking North American exposure at a discount to sum-of-the-parts.

headline: IAMGOLD Q2: CÔTÉ GOLD ONTARIO DRIVES MINE-SITE FREE CASH FLOW UP 290% — 188,100 OZ PRODUCED, GUIDANCE ON TRACK
snippet: IAMGOLD Corporation (TSX: IMG; NYSE: IAG) reported Q2 2026 results on August 6, 2026, with total attributable gold production of 188,100 ounces against 2026 annual guidance of 720,000–820,000 ounces — on track through mid-year. The headline number for investors is mine-site free cash flow of $368.9 million in Q2 alone, bringing year-to-date mine-site FCF to $893.5 million — a 290% increase versus the same period in 2025, driven almost entirely by the ramp-up of Côté Gold in Ontario. Côté produced 96,200 ounces on a 100% basis in Q2 (IAMGOLD holds 70%), with June processing costs falling to $17.72 per tonne following replacement of the main conveyor belt in May and commissioning of the second cone crusher — plant performance now approaching full capacity. Q3 and Q4 2026 production at Côté is guided higher than Q2 as the operational improvements compound. Côté is significant for retail investors tracking Canadian gold because it is the largest new gold mine built in Canada in this decade, reaching commercial production in May 2024 after years of construction and financing challenges. With the operational commissioning issues now largely resolved and production costs declining through throughput improvement, Côté at $4,300 gold is generating cash flow at multiples of its original feasibility assumptions — a demonstration of operating leverage from project completion at depressed gold prices followed by production at elevated prices.

headline: GOLIATH GOT.V SUREBET: GOLDEN TRIANGLE BC DISCOVERY EXPANDS IN THREE DIRECTIONS — GD-26-418 HITS 74.67 g/t AuEq PEAK
source_name: Mining News North / Goliath Resources (TSXV: GOT)
snippet: Goliath Resources Ltd. (TSXV: GOT; OTCQX: GOTRF) reported August 6, 2026 initial 2026 assay results from seven rigs drilling its fully funded 50,000-metre program at the Golddigger Property in BC's Golden Triangle, confirming simultaneous expansion of the Surebet Discovery's Bonanza Zone and Golden Gate Zone in multiple directions. Headline intercept GD-26-418 returned 8.09 g/t AuEq over 16.00 metres, including 74.67 g/t AuEq over 1.10 metres within the Bonanza Zone; the same hole cut 4.42 g/t AuEq over 5.00 metres in a separate nearby zone. The Golden Gate Zone now extends approximately 1.6 kilometres east-west and 1.5 kilometres north-south — still open in every direction — within the 1.8 km² Surebet Discovery footprint. Of the 35 holes drilled in the 2026 programme so far, 20 have intersected visible gold, indicating that the entire discovery area is mineralised rather than confined to discrete narrow veins. The 50,000-metre programme is less than halfway complete, leaving substantial upside from remaining assays across the 2026 campaign. The Golden Triangle has produced some of the world's highest-grade gold discoveries of the past decade — Seabridge KSM, Pretium Brucejack, GT Gold — and Surebet's multi-directional expansion with visible gold in 57% of drill holes positions it as one of the most active high-grade discovery programmes currently underway in Canada.

headline: TOCVAN VENTURES TOC.CN SONORA: 215m @ 0.6 g/t NEW MEZQUITE ZONE — 1.9KM FROM PLANNED PILOT PRODUCTION FACILITY
source_name: Investing News Network / Tocvan Ventures (CSE: TOC)
snippet: Tocvan Ventures Corp. (CSE: TOC; OTCQB: TCVNF) announced August 6, 2026 one of the best drill intercepts in its history at its 100%-owned Gran Pilar project in Sonora, Mexico: hole JES-26-155 returned 215 metres at 0.6 g/t gold from 36.6 metres downhole — a near-surface, bulk-tonnage intercept along the El Mezquite trend, a 1.2-kilometre mineralised corridor that begins 1,900 metres east of Tocvan's planned pilot production facility. The intercept breaks into an upper zone of 86.9 metres at 0.6 g/t gold and a lower zone of 70.2 metres at 0.9 g/t gold separated by anomalous material, with three high-grade intervals within the main intercept reaching up to 16.0 g/t gold and 57 g/t silver over 1.5 metres. This is a new zone — not previously modelled in any resource estimate — and its location along existing road infrastructure 1.9 kilometres from the planned pilot plant gives it immediate logistical significance: a 215-metre near-surface gold column within trucking range of infrastructure already under development is a materially different proposition than a remote discovery. Tocvan has now completed 10,098 metres of drilling at Gran Pilar in 2026, with additional assays from the El Mezquite trend outstanding. At current gold prices, an open-pit amenable, near-surface gold-silver system in Sonora Mexico within truck distance of planned processing infrastructure is among the more attractive junior exploration configurations for retail investors seeking district-scale upside at development-stage risk.

headline: ENERGY FUELS EFR: FIRST TERBIUM OXIDE EVER PRODUCED IN US CONFIRMED AT WHITE MESA — URANIUM OUTPUT 740K LBS YTD
source_name: Energy Fuels Inc (TSX: EFR / NYSE American: UUUU)
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (TSX: EFR; NYSE American: UUUU) reported Q2 2026 results on August 5, 2026 highlighting dual milestones in uranium and rare earth production at the White Mesa Mill in Utah — the only conventional uranium processing facility in the United States and the only US facility licensed to separate rare earth oxides from monazite. On the uranium side: 315,000 pounds of U3O8 mined at Pinyon Plain, La Sal, and Pandora in Q2 brings the year-to-date total to 740,000 pounds — within the company's 2026 annual guidance range of 1.5–2.5 million pounds with two quarters remaining. On the rare earth side: the March 2026 achievement of first US primary production of terbium oxide (Tb2O3) was confirmed — a historically significant milestone as the US had zero domestic primary terbium production before this. Terbium, alongside dysprosium, is one of the two rarest and most strategically critical rare earth elements due to its irreplaceable role in high-temperature permanent magnets; its domestic production removes one critical link in the US defense supply chain currently sourced entirely from China. White Mesa's rare earth expansion to add commercial-scale dysprosium and terbium circuits is on track for late 2027. The Q2 net loss of $33.4 million reflects transaction costs from planned acquisitions and the Phase 1 rare earth expansion capex — a development-stage cost profile at a company generating $80.48/lb uranium revenue against a spot price of $86.50/lb.

headline: EIA REPORT: US URANIUM OUTPUT TRIPLED TO 2.1M LBS IN 2025 — BUT STILL JUST 7% OF WHAT AMERICAN REACTORS NEED
source_name: Discovery Alert / U.S. Energy Information Administration
snippet: The U.S. Energy Information Administration's 2025 Uranium Marketing Annual Report, released in August 2026, provides the most comprehensive government data point yet on the gap between America's nuclear fuel ambitions and its domestic production reality. The headline finding: US uranium mines produced 2,109 thousand pounds of U3O8 in 2025 — a significant and credible production increase from 657,000 pounds in 2024 — but total US reactor purchases in 2025 were 46.9 million pounds of U3O8 equivalent, meaning domestic production covered approximately 4.5% of reactor needs. Accounting for domestic processing and secondary sources, the domestic contribution rises to roughly 7% — still 93% foreign-dependent. Canada (approximately 30%) and Kazakhstan (approximately 30%) together supplied 60% of all uranium delivered to US reactors in 2025. The EIA report also notes that exploration and development drilling in 2025 reached the highest level since 2013 by both holes drilled and total footage — confirming that capital is responding to price signals ($86.50/lb spot in August 2026, +20% year-on-year) but also confirming that US domestic supply cannot meaningfully close the gap with demand within a three-to-five year horizon given lead times for new mine development. For retail investors in US-listed or Canadian uranium companies, the EIA data quantifies the structural supply deficit that the spot price is already reflecting: 2.1 million pounds of domestic production against 46.9 million pounds of demand is not a near-term solvable problem, which is the fundamental floor under uranium prices.

headline: CHILE COPPER WINDFALL TOPS $9B AS LME HITS $14,000 — PRIVATE MINERS' RECORD STATE CONTRIBUTION IN 2026
snippet: Chile's Ministry of Finance projects fiscal revenues from large-scale private mining at approximately US$8–9 billion in 2026 — potentially the largest single-year tax and royalty take from private miners in Chilean history — as the London Metal Exchange copper price passed US$14,000 per tonne in early August and reached US$14,369.50 at intraday peaks. Copper generated US$19.053 billion in export revenue between January and April 2026 alone (80.8% of total Chilean mining export revenues), and Cochilco has raised its 2026 average copper price forecast to $5.90 per pound from $5.46 — a forecast trajectory that began 2026 below $4.00/lb and has been revised upward six times in nine months. The record government revenue arrives against a backdrop of production challenges: Cochilco projects Chilean 2026 output at 5.3 million tonnes, down 2% from 2025, as ore grade declines at mature Escondida, Collahuasi, and El Teniente deposits compound the capacity reduction from the El Teniente Andes Norte suspension. This creates a structurally unusual fiscal environment — record government copper receipts from price appreciation during a year when physical production is falling — that illustrates the commodity price leverage available to Chilean mining assets at $14,000/tonne copper. For junior copper developers in tariff-exempt jurisdictions (Canada under CUSMA, Australia under AUSFTA), the Chile data makes visible the type of government revenue and fiscal incentive structure that attaches to copper assets when prices are sustained above $13,000-$14,000/tonne.

headline: COMEX SILVER SPECULATORS STILL AT JUST 11,974 CONTRACTS NET LONG AS PRICE HITS $65 — POSITIONING LEAVES MAJOR RUNWAY
snippet: The CFTC Commitments of Traders report for the week ended August 4, 2026 — published August 7 — revealed that managed money speculators held only 11,974 net long contracts in COMEX silver futures as silver spot prices were trading near $64-65 per ounce, the highest level since the January all-time high complex. The positioning number is the analytically significant detail: at prior silver price peaks (January 2026 at all-time highs, and the 2020 retail silver squeeze), speculative net long positioning in COMEX silver ranged from 45,000 to 80,000+ contracts — three to seven times the current level. The gap between price performance (silver +65% year-on-year, near multi-decade highs) and speculative positioning (still near multi-year lows relative to price) is an unusual configuration that market analysts interpret as a fundamental demand-driven rally rather than a speculative blow-off: the move is being made with commercial and institutional buyers, while managed money is still significantly underweight silver relative to historical bull market positioning levels. Meanwhile, gold managed money positioning of 130,766 net long contracts confirms a reconstructing speculative position in gold — but one that remains below the 200,000+ contracts seen at January 2026 highs. The COMEX data adds quantitative structure to the silver bull market thesis: a commodity trading +65% year-on-year with speculative positioning at 15-25% of what it would typically carry at these price levels represents latent positioning demand that has not yet entered the market.

headline: GOLD EAGLE BULL MARKET ANALYSIS: 'THE NEXT HALF BEGINS' — $4,900+ TARGET SET AS CORRECTION ANATOMY CONFIRMED COMPLETE
snippet: Technical analyst AG Thorson published an August 5, 2026 analysis at Gold Eagle and FXEmpire identifying gold's recovery from the July low near $3,800 as the completion of the mid-cycle correction that marks the halfway point of the current secular gold bull market — the structural division between the first half (driven by institutional allocation and central bank buying) and the second half (historically led by mining stocks and retail investor participation). Thorson argues that the July 2026 correction — a 27.1% peak-to-trough decline from January's $5,598 all-time high — aligns precisely with the corrective structure seen at the midpoint of every major gold bull market of the past 50 years (1976 correction during the 1971–1980 bull, 2008 correction during the 2001–2011 bull, and 2013 correction during the structural gold advance from 2015). The second-half target range cited is $4,900–$5,200, with mining stocks — particularly junior gold equities — expected to substantially outperform bullion as the retail investor participation phase begins. The analysis emphasises that the strongest first-half signal is gold's ability to hold above $4,300 on a weekly close basis following the payrolls catalyst, which was achieved on August 7. For retail investors who held junior mining positions through the July correction or initiated positions during the drawdown, the structural bull market context argues that the pain of the correction was the price paid for entry ahead of the historically strongest phase of the cycle.
